beats.lead: The story everyone tells about kanban
beats.text: Taiichi Ohno saw an American supermarket called Piggly Wiggly, and that is where the idea came from.
beats.note: That version is repeated across the same blog posts and training decks. Ohno never named Piggly Wiggly in his own writing.

beats.name: Taiichi Ohno
beats.role: Toyota engineer shown photographs of an American supermarket by a colleague who had just returned from a US trip.

beats.text: Ohno named and began running his 'supermarket system' on Toyota's shop floor in 1952 and 1953: parts restocked only as they were withdrawn, the way a shelf is restocked after a customer takes something off it.
beats.note: He built the system from a description and photographs, years before he saw an American supermarket in person.

beats.text: By the time Ohno finally stood inside a US supermarket, in 1956, his system had already been running for three years.

beats.line: The supermarket came after the idea, not before it.
